items.followUp: Define boiling point and describe two factors that affect it.

accept: pressure of vapour in equilibrium with liquid
rubric.why: A definition must identify vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.description: Defines vapour pressure as the pressure exerted by a vapour in equilibrium with its liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the equilibrium pressure definition.

rubric.why: Increasing temperature gives more liquid molecules enough energy to escape into the vapour phase.
rubric.description: States that vapour pressure increases with temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct direction of the temperature effect.

rubric.why: Liquids with weaker intermolecular attractions vaporize more readily and have higher vapour pressure.
rubric.description: Relates the nature of the liquid or its intermolecular forces to vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct comparison or relationship.

rubric.why: A dissolved non-volatile substance reduces the tendency of solvent molecules to escape into the vapour phase.
rubric.description: States that a dissolved non-volatile impurity or solute lowers vapour pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct effect of a non-volatile solute.

modelAnswer: Vapour pressure is the pressure exerted by a vapour when it is in equilibrium with its liquid in a closed container.
A rise in temperature increases vapour pressure because more molecules escape from the liquid.
The nature of the liquid affects vapour pressure: weaker intermolecular forces give higher vapour pressure, while stronger forces give lower vapour pressure.
A dissolved non-volatile impurity lowers the vapour pressure of a liquid.

items.followUp: Define chemical change and give one example.

rubric.why: Chemical properties describe a substance's ability to undergo reactions and form new substances.
rubric.description: Defines chemical properties in terms of how a substance reacts or changes chemically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: A suitable example shows a substance undergoing a chemical reaction.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a chemical property or reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example.

modelAnswer: Chemical properties describe how a substance reacts chemically to form new substances.
For example, iron reacts with oxygen and moisture to form rust.

items.followUp: Write the chemical formulas of baking soda and slaked lime.

rubric.why: Washing soda is sodium carbonate decahydrate.
rubric.description: Writes the formula of washing soda.
Writes the formula of quick lime.

modelAnswer: Washing soda: Na2CO3·10H2O.
Quick lime: CaO.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of an element having 17 electrons.

rubric.why: The shell distribution for 11 electrons is 2 in the first shell, 8 in the second, and 1 in the third.
The subshell configuration accounts for all 11 electrons.

modelAnswer: An atom with 11 electrons has shell configuration 2, 8, 1.
Its subshell configuration is 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s1.

items.followUp: State two limitations of Bohr's atomic model.

rubric.why: According to classical theory, an orbiting electron should radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus; Rutherford's model could not explain why atoms remain stable.
rubric.description: Identifies that the model could not explain atomic stability or why electrons do not spiral into the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the stability defect.

rubric.why: The model did not explain the discrete line spectra emitted by atoms.
rubric.description: Identifies that the model could not explain atomic line spectra.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the spectrum defect.

modelAnswer: It could not explain the stability of the atom: an orbiting electron should lose energy and spiral into the nucleus.
It could not explain the line spectra of atoms.

items.followUp: Define electronegativity and state its trend across a period.

rubric.why: Electron affinity is the energy change, conventionally described as energy released, when an electron is added to a gaseous atom.
rubric.description: Defines electron affinity for the addition of an electron to a gaseous atom.

rubric.why: Across a period, electron affinity generally increases as effective nuclear attraction for an added electron increases.
rubric.description: States the general trend of electron affinity across a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it generally increases from left to right.

modelAnswer: Electron affinity is the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom to form a negative ion.
In general, electron affinity increases from left to right across a period.

items.followUp: Define second ionization energy and write the ionization equation for magnesium's first ionization.

rubric.why: First ionization energy is the energy needed to remove the most loosely held electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the gaseous-atom electron-removal definition.

rubric.why: The first ionization energy of sodium is approximately 496 kJ mol−1 (about 5.14 eV per atom).
rubric.description: Gives the first ionization energy of sodium with a unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 496 kJ mol−1 or its equivalent.

modelAnswer: First ionization energy is the energy required to remove the most loosely held electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
Na(g) → Na+(g) + e−; first ionization energy of sodium = 496 kJ mol−1.

items.followUp: Identify the covalent bond type in O2, C2H6, CO2 and Cl2.

rubric.why: H2 has one shared pair, and each C–H bond in CH4 is a single covalent bond.
rubric.description: Identifies the bonds in H2 and CH4 as single covalent bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both molecules are correctly identified as having single bonds.

rubric.why: Ethene contains a C=C double bond, while N2 contains an N≡N triple bond.
rubric.description: Identifies the bonds in C2H4 and N2 as double and triple, respectively.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark when both molecules are correctly identified.

modelAnswer: H2: single covalent bond.
CH4: single covalent bonds.
C2H4: double covalent bond between the carbon atoms.
N2: triple covalent bond.
